newsitem.title: CROATIA: Polls open in Croatia's municipal elections.
newsitem.headline: Polls open in Croatia's municipal elections.

text.p: Polling stations across Croatia opened on Sunday for voters to cast their ballots in the first local and Upper House elections since the end of the war.

Some 3.6 million voters, including the Serbs in the separatist region of Eastern Slavonia, will vote to fill more than 10,000 seats at all levels of powers, from local municipal assemblies to the House of Counties -- the upper house of the Croatian parliament, the Sabor.
Polling stations opened at 7 a.m. local time (0500 GMT), and will close 12 hours later. Hundreds of United Nations and other international observers will judge whether the vote is free and fair.

The elections are seen as a crucial test for the volatile Eastern Slavonia region, where local Serbs are taking part in a vote organised by Zagreb for the first time since they rebelled against Croatian independence in 1991.

The region, now controlled by some 5,000 U.N. troops, is to revert to the government control in mid July, but many Serbs are considering leaving despite the official guarantees, fearing retribution by thousands of Croatian refugees expelled during the 1991-95 war.
The poll is also an important test of popularity for President Franjo Tudjman, who faces re-election later this year, and his ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ).
Recent independent polls showed the HDZ trailing behind the cetre-left opposition in many cities, including the capital Zagreb.

The HDZ is faced with losing power in Zagreb, if it fails to win at least a relative majority, which would give the autocratic 74-year old president an excuse to prevent the opposition naming a mayor, as he did in 1995.
A fervent anti-communist campaign in the state-run media suggests the HDZ fears it could lose to the Social Democrats (reformed communists) in Zagreb.
This would be their first victory since losing power in the former Yugoslav republic's first free and democratic elections in 1990.
